solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, mirror symmetry); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Regret absence of girl

definitions.meaning: to feel the lack of someone or something and wish it back
a title for a young unmarried woman, so a girl

explanation.surface: Someone sorry that a particular girl is not around.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a verb for pining over what is gone, and the courtesy title for a young woman.

clue.text: Teacher upset US uncle — schooltime cut short

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, so it is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a term is a period of school time

explanation.surface: A teacher annoys an American relative by ending the school period early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SAM into MAS; 'cut short' trims TERM to TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a teacher, and the shorter title is used the same way.

clue.text: It's funny: initially, staff in television companies order more

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Staff at TV firms want more of a comedy that amuses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a television show designed to be funny, so 'it's funny' describes one.

clue.text: Italy not entirely enthralled by upper limits in London and Paris, say?

indicators.note: being enthralled by something is being held captive inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: caps are upper limits, as on spending

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is given without its last letter

explanation.surface: A question of whether Italy is fully gripped by limits imposed in two great cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the last letter of Italy; 'upper limits' reads as caps on spending, and 'enthralled by' puts the shortened country inside.
explanation.definitionFit: London and Paris are examples of national seats of government; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Fuss today upset nurses

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, so they read from the bottom up
a word that nurses something holds it within, so the letters are found inside today

explanation.surface: Nurses kick up a fuss because they are upset today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' points to letters held inside 'today', and 'upset' turns them round to read ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do or commotion; 'much ado about nothing' is fuss over nothing.

clue.text: Offence if the tidy tent toppled

indicators.note: toppled means knocked over and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A camper wondering whether knocking over a neat tent counts as a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing someone's personal details to pose as them is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Irish graduate invested in silver safety device

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: An Irish graduate puts money into silver as a kind of security.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion that inflates in a car crash is a protective device for occupants.

clue.text: After losing heart, saw ideal garden in country

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Eden is the perfect garden of Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone dispirited after seeing a perfect garden in rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After losing heart' takes the middle A from saw, leaving SW.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation, so an example of a country.

clue.text: New vet too costly (not half!) — whispered in undertone

indicators.note: new means made over afresh, so the letters are rearranged
not half means only the first half of the word, three letters of six, is used

explanation.surface: A new vet's fees are too steep, someone mutters quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' keeps COS from costly; with VET and TOO, 'New' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase means literally 'under the voice', i.e. spoken quietly so as not to be overheard.

clue.text: Strange to revere a binger

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It seems odd to look up to someone who indulges excessively.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who binges eats far too much in one go, a glutton.

clue.text: Sussex port grass

definitions.meaning: An old harbour town in East Sussex, a county on England's south coast
a cereal plant of the grass family grown for grain

explanation.surface: A seaside town's lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves a south-coast English town and a cereal grass.

clue.text: Back Eastern European with energy in run off

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, in Eastern Europe
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An Eastern European fled with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern European' is one unit naming a nationality, not E plus a separate word; 'Back' reverses it before the energy symbol follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off to marry secretly are said to do so.

clue.text: Modest dwelling, firm, dry, linked with particular period

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
an age is a particular period of history

explanation.surface: An estate-agent listing for a small home, with a company, a dry spell and an era.
explanation.definitionFit: A small simple house, typically in the country, is a modest dwelling.

clue.text: Tea with politician — winner

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A cuppa with an MP to celebrate a victor.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal short form of champion, someone who has won.

clue.text: Great at tricky races in water

indicators.note: tricky means awkward or twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone excellent at difficult boat contests.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of rowing or sailing races held on a river or sea.

clue.text: Declare categorically: "Right to participate in something useful"

indicators.note: one who participates in something goes inside it, so this letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: an asset is a useful thing

explanation.surface: A firm statement that it is right to join in a worthwhile project.
explanation.definitionFit: To state firmly and confidently is to declare something as fact.

clue.text: Look around pages for spicy stuff?

indicators.note: around means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Leafing through a book in search of racy passages.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot seasoning ground from peppercorns, an example of something spicy.

clue.text: Insincere talk about Swiss region

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, pious talk
on means concerning or about

explanation.surface: Hollow chatter concerning an area of Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is divided into administrative districts with this name, like Zurich or Geneva.

clue.text: Courage of copper, perhaps (pronounced)

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word sounds like the one given

parts.note: copper is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: A query about whether a policeman, maybe, is brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer; here it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit and resilience under pressure; to show one's mettle is to prove one's bravery.

clue.text: He cuts firm leaf

indicators.note: something that cuts into a word splits it, sitting in the middle

parts.note: set means firm, as a jelly sets
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man slicing a tough leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf of paper is a single sheet of it.

clue.text: Main object of dislike in Europe — that extremist

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: The chief thing hated in Europe is that extremist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate is one's particular bugbear, the thing most loathed.

clue.text: Former forward is beginning to exhibit special skill

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
pert means cheeky, forward

indicators.note: beginning to means take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A one-time striker starting to show particular talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Expert knowledge or a high level of proficiency in some area.

clue.text: Diamonds more pleasant with wrappers removed

indicators.note: wrappers are the outer letters, so the word loses its first and last

parts.note: nicer means more pleasant

explanation.surface: Gems look better unwrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, from their glassy sparkle.

clue.text: Drink at most intermittently

indicators.note: intermittently means taking every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Someone who drinks only now and then, at the most.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits, a drink.

clue.text: At end of circuit, vessel to change course

indicators.note: end of means take the final letter of the word

parts.note: an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A racing car finishing a lap and swerving off line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat but is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn is to change direction.

clue.text: Judgment dispatched in French church

parts.note: sent means dispatched
en is French for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A verdict delivered in a French church.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's sentence is its judgment on the punishment due.
